xmlRec.title: Phase 3 semaglutide randomized controlled trial.
xmlRec.abstract: METHODS: In this phase 3 trial, 1200 patients with obesity were randomly assigned to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo for 68 weeks. The coprimary end points were the percentage change in body weight and weight reduction of at least 5%. RESULTS: With semaglutide, mean body weight reduction was -14.9% and weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 86.4% vs 31.5% (95% CI 11.2 to 13.7; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide led to clinically meaningful weight reductions.
